rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a transfer-worthy expanded blastocyst and appropriately notes uncertainty from a single still image, but it questions the reported 3AA and describes ICM/TE heterogeneity without clear image-grounded certainty.
Integrates key factors well: young age, good endometrium, male factor diagnosis, BMI, ovarian reserve, first cycle, and semen parameters, with reasonable discussion of how these affect prognosis.
Reasoning is logical and internally consistent overall, with probability estimates tied to embryo quality and patient factors; only minor overinterpretation of image-vs-grade discordance.

Recommendations are largely evidence-based and aligned with common IVF practice, including single embryo transfer at age 31 and avoiding unnecessary adjuvants; minor speculative elements reduce a perfect score.
Provides practical next steps for transfer, luteal support, lifestyle, and future-cycle review, though some suggestions remain somewhat general rather than protocol-specific.
